jobs.occupation: 1352 Postdoctoral position in marine ecological modelling
jobs.description:
About the Position
The Institute of Marine Research (IMR) offers a 3-year postdoctoral position as part of the MORSE (“Models supporting practical restoration of habitats and species in Europe’s seas”) research project funded by Horizon Europe. This project sits within IMR’s strategic initiative to build a strong center for marine research within one of Europe's largest marine research institutes. The candidate will ideally start in early 2027. 

We seek a postdoctoral researcher with a background in ecological modelling, with relevant experience and publication record on modelling marine and/or aquatic ecosystems. The postdoctoral researcher will work across several work packages, including WP5 (reviewing and compiling data on restoration pathways, pressures, and ecological needs of focal species and habitats, and defining favourable reference areas), WP6 (species distribution modelling and assessment of environmental status (NEAT), WP7 (modelling land-, and sea-based pressures, and MPAs), and WP8 (modelling ecosystem services). The broader aim of the project is to develop and demonstrate effective and climate-resilient restoration models for European marine ecosystems to inform more effective restoration efforts. 

The postdoctoral researcher will work with a team of researchers at IMR and collaborating partners to carry out and deliver research outcomes in the MORSE project. The MORSE project that the postdoctoral position is associated with is a 4-year project that is led by the Finnish Environmental Institute (SYKE) and includes institutions across seven European countries (Finland, Sweden, Norway, UK, Spain, Portugal, and Greece). Travel to workshops and meetings in these countries should be anticipated. The postdoctoral researcher will gain mentoring support, training, and networking opportunities from the leading researchers associated with the MORSE project, and have the opportunity to establish connections and advance their research career over the course of the project. More information about MORSE can be found at the project website: https://morse-project.eu/ 

Knowledge about northern European marine ecosystems is an advantage, as the postdoctoral researcher will be responsible for modelling Norwegian marine ecosystems. The position is placed within the Benthic Communities research group and can be located at any of the IMR offices. Note that the IMR project lead (Karine Gagnon) is based at Flødevigen Research Station, but the research group includes members across all three locations. IMR has good links and cooperation with industry, management, and the university sector. We offer the opportunity to be part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary, and ambitious research group with strong national and international links.

Main tasks:

• Lead and support MORSE research activities as directed by project leaders. 
• Write research publications, reports, and grant proposals.
• Participate in scientific conferences, science communication, and outreach activities. 
• Review and compile existing data on restoration pathways, ecosystem status, and pressures for focal species and habitats, and define favourable reference areas for these 
• Review and compile existing models and data sources for the Norwegian sea areas (including the Skagerrak, Norwegian Sea, North Sea, and Barents Sea) 
• Apply species distribution models and assess environmental status using the NEAT tool 
• Model land-based and sea-based pressures on marine habitats, and the role of MPAs 
• Model climate scenarios and ecosystem services 
• Participate in work package coordination and reporting 
• Maintain and curate datasets and coordinate data sharing and modelling efforts across MORSE partners.About the Research Group and Our Work
The Benthic Communities group focuses on research, mapping, and monitoring of benthic ecosystems, including seagrass meadows, macroalgae forests, and deep-sea ecosystems. Research within the project will support IMR’s national advisory task on ecosystem-based management of seas and coastal areas, where environmental changes and human activities and are important factors. The research group has over 30 employees base on Flødevigen, Bergen, and Tromsø.
Qualification Requirements
For this position, we are looking for a candidate with

• PhD in biology or ecology, preferably with a focus on ecological modelling
• Documented experience in ecological modelling 
• Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral skills in English
The working language at the Institute of Marine Research is Norwegian. Being able to communicate well in Norwegian is an important prerequisite for both the employee and our institute. We expect non-Norwegian-speaking employees to complete Norwegian language courses during the first two years of employment. The institute will cover the cost of completed and passed Norwegian courses.
Personal Qualities
At the Institute of Marine Research, we believe that personality plays a role in how one works, communicates, and thrives in the workplace. For this position, we are looking for a colleague who

• Good communication and collaboration skills. 
• Good organisational and logistics skills. 
• Ability to complete work on time and meeting deadline 
• Ability to work efficiently independently and in teams.Desired Qualifications
• Strong skills and experience in ecological modelling and data analysis
• Ability and willingness to collaborate with colleagues in Norway and abroad 
• Ability and willingness to organize and lead joint modelling efforts with partners abroad 
• Research experience in marine ecosystems, species, and habitats 
• Research experience in ecological restoration and/or conservationInclusion and Diversity is a Strength
The Institute of Marine Research believes that inclusion and diversity are strengths. Therefore, we encourage all qualified candidates to apply for a position with us, regardless of age, gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic background. The Institute is an Inclusive Workplace (IA) company, and we aim to accommodate applicants with disabilities.

If there are qualified applicants with disabilities, employment gaps, or immigrant backgrounds, we will invite at least one applicant from each of these groups to an interview. To be considered for affirmative action, you must meet the requirements and indicate that you wish to be considered for the action in your application. You can read more here.
Your application must include 
• a cover letter describing your research interests and motivation for applying for the position. The letter should not exceed one A4 page.• Full name and contact details for two or three referees, preferably your PhD supervisor and/or references from recent employment.• CV, transcripts, diplomas, and relevant certificates.• A list of scientific publications, if applicable.

All documents must be in a Scandinavian language or in English. Candidates with documentation from foreign institutions must include an explanation of the institution’s grading system.
We offer
• the opportunity to work in one of Europe’s leading marine research institutes
• a creative working environment
• facilities in either Flødevigen, Bergen or Tromsø 
• flexible work hours 
• public sector occupational pension through the Norwegian Public Service Pension Funds (SPK)
• access to company cabins, fitness facilities, and other welfare benefitsAditional information
The position is remunerated as 1352 Postdoctoral in accordance with the main collective agreement in the state sector, depending on your qualifications and the characteristics of the position. A 2 % contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted from the salary.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Jobbnorge.

Please note that information about applicants may be made public even if the applicant has requested not to be listed. Applicants will be informed in advance if such disclosure is necessary.

The Institute of Marine Research is subject to export control regulations. These regulations apply to the processing of applications for the position.

Applicants with education from abroad may be asked to provide NOKUT approval of their qualifications. You may be asked to approve that the Institute of Marine Research conducts a background check.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The Institute of Marine Research is one of Europe’s largest marine research institutes, with over 1,000 employees and a range of high-standard research facilities and laboratories. Our main activities are research, advisory work, and monitoring. The institute owns and operates eight research vessels. Our headquarters are in Bergen, with additional offices in Tromsø and research stations in Matre, Austevoll, and Flødevigen.The Institute of Marine Research aims to be a leading provider of knowledge to ensure the sustainable management of marine ecosystem resources—nationally and internationally—across the entire value chain from ocean to food, including the marine environment, fish nutrition, and safe, healthy seafood.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Political Science - Norway and the EU
jobs.description:
About the position 
ARENA Centre for European Studies at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position as PhD Research Fellow (SKO 1017) in political science or another relevant social science discipline. The position is for a period of three years, with no teaching or other required duties. 

The place of work is ARENA Centre for European Studies, University of Oslo.
 
ARENA is an interdisciplinary research centre at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. Since 1994, the centre has studied political, security, economic, legal and social integration, transformation and cooperation in Europe. ARENA has extensive experience in coordinating international research projects and networks funded by European and Norwegian institutions. 

The centre has around 30 academic and four administrative staff. More information about ARENA is available here.
More about the position 
Europe is being reshaped by war, geopolitical rivalry and a renewed enlargement agenda. As the EU's rules and decisions reach further beyond its borders, Norway faces key questions about alignment, influence and democratic control. Norway is one of the most closely integrated non-member states. That makes it an important case for understanding what it means to be part of European integration without being a member of the Union.

ARENA is looking for a PhD Research Fellow who wants to write a dissertation on Norway's relationship with the EU. The successful candidate will develop and carry out their own doctoral project in a research environment with long experience of studying European integration and its consequences for countries both inside and outside the Union.

We expect theoretically informed empirical studies and particularly welcome projects that take a comparative approach, but single-case studies of Norway are also welcome. Examples of comparisons could include comparing and contrasting Norway with other associated or third countries (such as Iceland, Switzerland or the United Kingdom), EU member states or candidate countries. Comparisons across policy areas are also welcome. We are open to a range of theoretical and methodological approaches.

Relevant research areas could include, but are not limited to:

• Norway's association model: Projects could for example address how the EEA Agreement and Norway's many other agreements with the EU shape Norwegian politics, public administration and regulation, or how they compare with those of comparable EU member or affiliated states. Projects could look at Norway's room for manoeuvre and influence vis-à-vis the EU, at questions of democratic legitimacy and control, or at how the association model is evolving as the EU changes. 
• Justice and home affairs: Projects could for example address Norway's participation in Schengen, European migration and asylum policy, border management, or police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. Projects could study how EU developments in these fields affect Norwegian policies, institutions and societal security, possibly compared with other associated or member countries.
We are looking for candidates with interesting and relevant research ideas, strong theoretical and analytical skills, and solid methodological competence. The project proposal should combine clear theoretical and empirical ambitions with a realistic and feasible research design.
Responsibilities
The appointment as a PhD Research Fellow at ARENA is for a period of three years, with no compulsory duties. As a fellow, you will be based at ARENA Centre for European Studies’ premises in Gaustadalléen, Oslo. Presence at the unit is a requirement. 

You will be admitted to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo.

This is a full-time position commencing in the winter or spring of 2027. You will have access to office space, equipment, and services, as well as resources for fieldwork and conference participation as needed.
What skills are important in this role?
Required selection criteria 

• The position requires a completed master's degree equivalent to a two-year programme (120 ECTS credits) within the social sciences, approved by the faculty as a basis for admission.
• Grades placing the candidate in the top tier of the field (this also applies to the master's thesis)
• The master's degree must include relevant training in research design and methodology
• The master's thesis must correspond to a minimum workload of six months, i.e., 30 ECTS credits
• 
Excellent oral and written English proficiency is required

ARENA’s working language is English, and therefore, fluency in oral and written English is required. As Norway’s relationship with the EU is central to the position, Norwegian sources will be important, making good proficiency in Norwegian (or another Scandinavian language) an advantage.
 
Personal suitability

• You must be able to work independently and in a structured manner.

• You should possess good collaborative skills and demonstrate the ability, willingness, and commitment to contribute to the development of the research field.

• 
You should be able to take initiative and wish to participate actively in an international and interdisciplinary research team.

Appointment as a research fellow requires admission to a doctoral programme, or a binding agreement regarding admission. 

Application for admission to a PhD programme must normally be submitted within three months of the start of the research project leading to the PhD degree. 
Basis for assessment
In the assessment of candidates, particular emphasis will be placed on:

(1) the quality and relevance of the project proposal

(2) academic qualifications (transcripts must be attached)

(3) the master's thesis and any other published work

(4) references.

Personal qualities and motivation will be taken into consideration.

Potential candidates will be invited to an interview.
We need different perspectives in our work 
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
We can offer you 
• Salary in positon as Research Fellow (job code 1017) in the range of NOK 550 800 to NOK 630 000, depending on qualifications and experience. A statutory
two per cent deduction is made from the salary for the mandatory contribution to the State Pension Fund.

• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organisation with an important societal mission

• An academically stimulating international research environment
• A pleasant and stimulating work environment
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours. 
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.
Application
Your application should include:

• Cover letter (maximum 1 000 words, approx. two pages), containing:
a brief description of yourself,
a brief description of your qualifications and relevant experience,
a brief description of your planned research project,
a brief explanation of why ARENA is of interest to you
• CV (please note that the duration from admission to completion of your master's programme must be specified)
• 
Project description (maximum 2 500 words, approx. six pages excluding the reference list), containing:
your research interests,
knowledge of previous research in the relevant field,
evidence of your ability to formulate scientific research questions,
specification of the relevant research design and methodology.
• 
Academic transcripts
• 
Up to two writing samples (e.g., master's thesis or published articles). Please note that there is no specific upload field
for such documents in the application portal. These must therefore be uploaded as a separate attachment.

• List of publications
• 

Contact information for 2–3 references

Your CV must be entered into the Jobbnorge CV form; it cannot simply be submitted as an attachment. This procedure ensures correct documentation and
record-keeping in accordance with Section 15 of the Regulations to the Public Administration Act.

The application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system, Jobbnorge; click “Apply for the position”. 

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
Contact information
For further information regarding the position please contact

Centre Director: Pernille Rieker,  ARENA
General information
Please note that we are unable to add documentation after the application deadline. As the deadline applies equally to all applicants, this policy ensures equal treatment throughout the recruitment process. If you experience difficulties uploading documents in Jobbnorge, please contact their customer service: Phone: +47 75 54 22 20 or Email: support@grade.com The primary method of communication throughout the process will be e-mails and messages through the recruitment system Jobbnorge. When you receive a notification of a message in Jobbnorge, please log in to read it, as it may be important.The best qualified candidates will invited for interviews. 
 
Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian), Guidelines concerning appointment to recruitment positions at UiO and Regulations for the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo.

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees to secure the rights to all research results and related intellectual property.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.

ARENA Centre for European Studies is a research centre under the Faculty of Social Sciences. ARENA promotes theoretically oriented, empirically informed studies analysing the dynamics of the evolving European political order. The research at ARENA is multidisciplinary and is organised along four key dimensions: A European democratic order; the EU's executive order; expertise and knowledge in the EU; and European foreign and security policy. ARENA hosts several nationally and internationally funded research projects and is engaged in a series of international networks.

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Geography and Social Anthropology offers a PhD Candidate position for a period of three years.The Department of Geography and Social Anthropology invites candidates to apply for a three-year position as a PhD Research Fellow in Geography with focus on Post-Fossil Fuel Transitions in Petroleum-Producing Nations. The PhD fellow will be part of the Research Group “Geographies of Just and Sustainable Transitions”, and will join a dynamic and collegial research environment that includes both early career and senior researchers working across a broad range of fields at the Department.The PhD fellow will also be affiliated with the NTNU Strategic Area on Energy under the focus area “Beyond the Fossil Fuel Era” and will be supervised by Alexander Dodge and co-supervised by Amber Nordholm and Espen Moe.Starting date as soon as possible/by agreement.Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The global oil and gas (O&G) sector sits at a critical conjuncture – there is broad consensus among governments, industry and market outlooks that global oil demand will plateau or peak between 2030 and 2035 as governments around the world work to meet their climate commitments and as new technologies (i.e. solar panels, heat pumps, batteries, etc.) gain traction in global markets. At the same time, however, the pace and speed of fossil fuel decline afterwards is highly uncertain. The Strait of Hormuz blockades have generated enormous revenue for O&G companies but may also prove to be an inflection point that accelerates efforts to move beyond fossil fuels. The uncertainty surrounding the future of fossil fuels is particularly prevalent for governments in petroleum-producing nations. On one hand, governments are under increasing pressure by the public and civil society organizations to end fossil fuel subsidies, stop new field exploration and development, and transition their economies away from fossil-fuel production. On the other hand, as the energy transition progresses, it has created its own counterforces and resulted in political pushback from climate-skeptical or even climate-denying political populists who have argued that the energy transition is inefficient, expensive, and unduly harming regular people, and that the only thing that protects the economy and preserves the welfare state is to open new areas for exploration and to provide tax relief/subsidies to stimulate new developments.The primary objective of the PhD project should be to investigate and better understand the contradictions and dilemmas democratic states in petroleum-producing nations must negotiate and navigate through uncertainty surrounding the direction and pace of transition to a post-fossil fuel era. Drawing energy geographies, (cultural) political economy and/or sustainability transitions, the successful candidate should examine the politics, strategies, counterforces, and/or backlashes surrounding statecraft in democratic petroleum-producing nations. This entails a focus on the role of and relationships between institutional legacies, vested interests, labor, expertise (consultants, think-tanks, academia, etc.) and/or civil society in shaping how the democratic-states conducts public affairs, initiates government projects, and manages domestic and international relations surrounding the petroleum-sector and fossil-fuel transitions.Successful candidates may choose to limit their study to the Norwegian-context or conduct a cross-comparative study between Norway and other democratic petroleum-producing nations such as United Kingdom, Indonesia, and Australia. Candidates should aim to contribute to discussions in national newspapers or public forums that could eventually feed into discussions surrounding the report from Norway’s Transition Commission (“Omstillingskommisjon”).

• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above

• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions.Be prepared for changes to your work duties during the employment period.Required selection criteria

• Your education must be equivalent to a five-year Norwegian degree.

If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.

Preferred selection criteria

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Resilient Service Continuity Across Mobile Networks
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you motivated to pursue a doctoral degree and explore how mobile networks can work together to keep critical services running when facing failures or congestion?

The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU has a vacancy for a PhD Candidate in Resilient Service Continuity Across Mobile Networks. As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a range of leading positions in business, administration, higher education and research.

The position is fully funded and will run for 4 years (100 % employment), including teaching duties. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Discipline, and the workplace will be in Trondheim.
About the project
Mobile networks increasingly support critical services in emergency response, industry, transport, and maritime operations. Access to several networks can improve resilience, but sustaining a service requires more than restoring connectivity. Independently operated networks must coordinate resources and priorities while managing dependencies and commitments to existing users. They may also depend on shared infrastructure or capacity leased from one another, limiting the resilience gained from access to multiple operators. Norway’s plans for a new emergency network (Nødnett) over commercial mobile infrastructure illustrate the relevance of these broader challenges.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how mobile networks can cooperate to maintain critical services during failures, congestion, and recovery. Your research will address networks that retain their own operational policies and exchange limited information about capacity and internal state, developing insights applicable across public and private networks. A specific focus will be on the networked systems mechanisms, data paths, and open interfaces needed to support resilient service continuity in multi-operator mobile network systems, addressing research questions such as:

• What information must networks exchange to make effective admission and resource-allocation decisions without requiring full visibility into each other’s infrastructure?
• How can service priorities and resource policies be coordinated across heterogeneous networks, including during congestion and large bursts of registration requests?
• How can network selection, traffic steering, and recovery mechanisms maintain application continuity while avoiding repeated switching and overload cascades?
• How do shared infrastructure, leased capacity, and dependencies between operators affect failure propagation and the resilience gained from alternative network access?
With the Beyond 5G lab at the department, the project will emphasize experimental systems research: you will have the opportunity to conduct your research in both commercial and open-source mobile network deployments and test your ideas under realistic conditions. To explore conditions beyond the scale of the physical deployments, methods including simulation and analytical modeling can be a complementary building block.
Duties of the position
• Complete doctoral education and obtain a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the Networking research group
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Teaching in courses related to networking
• Other career-enhancing work
Some changes to your work duties may occur after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in Information Security and Communication Technology, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant master's degree in communication networks, wireless and mobile communications, information security and distributed systems, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and preferably within August 2027.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• If you are in your master’s program, integrated PhD could be an option. Your MSc grades after your fourth year need to be completed with a grade B or better, in addition the IE-faculty require that your bachelor degree is completed with a grade C or better. Integrated PhD - Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering - NTNU.
• Excellent oral and written presentation skills in English.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Practical experience with 5G radio access and core deployments.
• Hands-on experience with communication networks including multi-vendor and softwarized environments.
• Exposure to resilience and dependability topics in the context of communication networks as part of the master’s curriculum.
• Teaching experience, preferably at master’s level.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are

• Highly motivated by fundamental scientific research with practical relevance.
• Able to work independently.
• Able to work in a structured way, set goals, and make plans to achieve them.
• Eager to disseminate research results both locally as well as through publications and presentations at international conferences.
In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal suitability, as well as motivation, in terms of the qualifications specified in the advertisement.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) 
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work in addition to one year of career promotion work.

The successful candidate will be granted conditional admission to the relevant doctoral programme when employed in the PhD position. It is a prerequisite for continued employment that the requirements for full admission are met within three months, and that you continue to participate in the organized doctoral programme for the remainder of the employment period. For more information about the requirements for full admission, please see Section 6 of the PhD regulations. 

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.

If you are invited for an interview, you must present certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If all, or parts of, your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both bachelor's and master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution does not offer “diploma supplement”, you must attach information about the grading scale from the education institution.

Follow the link to their web site for more information about how to obtain such a statement: Apply for recognition of foreign higher education. See also NTNU’s web site for documentation requirements for education obtained outside Norway. 

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information

You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.If you have any questions about the position, please contact Associate Professor Stanislav Lange, e-mail: stanislav.lange@ntnu.no.

Om stillingen
En stipendiatstilling innen kjønnsstudier er ledig på Senter for kvinne- og kjønnsforskning (SKK) ved Institutt for filosofi og førstesemesterstudier (IFF), Fakultet for humaniora, samfunnsvitenskap og lærerutdanning (HSL), UiT Norges arktiske universitet. Stillingen er knyttet til forskningssatsingen Gender, A Iand Technological Engagements (GATE): Towards Informed Futures, ledetav Ania Malinowska. 

Den som ansettes, skal utvikle og gjennomføre et selvstendig doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor GATEs tematiske ramme, med sikte på å oppnå ph.d.-graden. Stipendiaten skal delta aktivt i forskningsmiljøet ved SKK og bidra til tverrfaglig kunnskapsutveksling om kjønn, kunstig intelligens, teknologisk utvikling og samfunnsliv.

Arbeidsstedet er campus Tromsø. Stillingen har en varighet på tre år, med mulighet for ett års forlengelse dersom doktorgradsavhandlingen leveres innen normert tid.

De høyest rangerte kandidatene kan forvente å bli innkalt til intervju innen april. Ønsket tiltredelse er i august 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen er en utdanningsstilling og har fullført forskerutdanning frem til doktorgrad som mål. Opptak til doktorgradsprogram er en forutsetning for ansettelse og studieperioden starter ved tiltredelse i stillingen.

Stillingen gjelder for en periode på 3 år og ph.d.-studier på fulltid med mulighet for forlengelse av et gjennomføringsstipend. Dersom doktoravhandlingen leveres på normert studietid innen 3 år eller innen 3,5 år, kvalifiserer stipendiaten seg for et gjennomføringsstipend på henholdsvis 12 eller 6 måneder. Gjennomføringsstipendet skal brukes til kvalifikasjonsfremmende tiltak inkl. universitetspedagogisk kurs, undervisning og andre arbeidsoppgaver ved fakultetet. Mer om ordningen med gjennomføringsstipend finner du her.

Veiledning og forskningsmiljø

Foreslått hovedveileder er førsteamanuensis Ania Malinowska, kulturteoretiker og forsker med kompetanse innen teknologi, affekt, kjønn og kultur. Forskningen hennes kombinerer kultur- og kjønnsteoretiske perspektiver med mediearkeologi, kvalitative metoder og kunstbasert eksperimentering. Hun er forfatter av Love in Contemporary Technoculture (Cambridge University Press) og Cutting Up Books:A Writing Method in Critical Thinking (Intellect), og medoppfinner av Hypnotic AI, et patentert KI-basert forsknings- og kunstsystem som undersøker affektive relasjoner mellom mennesker og teknologi. 

Formelle veiledningsavtaler vil bli fastsatt i tråd med UiTs regelverk for doktorgradsutdanning.
Om prosjektet / Stillingens forskningsområde
Gender, AI and Technological Engagements (GATE) bringer kjønnsforskning i dialog med teknologi- og vitenskapsstudier (STS), kritiske KI-studier, affektteori og digital humaniora. Prosjektet undersøker hvordan forståelser av kjønn påvirker utvikling, bruk og styring av intelligente systemer, og hvordan disse systemene i sin tur former identiteter, affekter, sosiale relasjoner, kunnskap, arbeid og deltakelse.

Prosjektet har en kritisk og konstruktiv tilnærming til kunstig intelligens (KI). Det undersøker hvordan KI og algoritmiske systemer kan reprodusere ulikhet, ekskludering og skjevheter, samt hvordan kjønnsforskning kan bidra til en mer inkluderende, rettferdig og sosialt ansvarlig teknologisk fremtid. Nordområdeneutgjør en viktig kontekst for å undersøke geografiske og språklige skjevheter i teknologiske systemer og for å utvikle tilnærminger som tar utgangspunkt i nordlige og arktiske erfaringer med og historier om teknologi. 

Søkere forventes å foreslå et avgrenset og gjennomførbart doktorgradsprosjekt som tar for seg én eller flere av følgende forskningsretninger:

• Kjønnede antakelser, representasjon og skjevheter i KI-systemer, datasett, plattformer og brukergrensesnitt.
• Kjønnsidentiteter og forventninger i samhandling med KI-agenter, roboter,avatarer og digitale assistenter.
• Affekt, tillit, intimitet, omsorg og relasjoner i møter mellom mennesker og maskiner.
• Algoritmiske tilbakekoblingssløyfer, dataekskludering og produksjon av kjønnet kunnskap.
• Kjønnede endringer i arbeidsliv, automatisering, ekspertise og sosial reproduksjon.
• Kjønnssensitive kvalitative, digitale, historiske, eksperimentelle eller kunstbaserte metoder for forskning på intelligente teknologier.
• Kjønnssensitiv teknologiutvikling, fremtidsstudier, styring og frigjørende muligheter.
• KI og teknologiske fremtider i nordområdene, inkludert minoritetsspråk, urfolkskontekster og geografiske ulikheter. 
Prosjektbeskrivelsen skal formulere en tydelig problemstilling, forankre denne i relevant kjønnsteoretisk forskning, identifisere egnede metoder og empirisk materiale, drøfte forskningsetiske spørsmål og presentere en realistisk plan for gjennomføring innenfor ansettelsesperioden. Prosjektet kan være teoretisk,empirisk eller praksisbasert, forutsatt at det viser et solid kjønnsteoretisk og/eller metodologisk bidrag.

Avhengig av doktorgradsprosjektets innretning kan forskningen omfatte kvalitativt feltarbeid, mediearkeologi, analyser av digitale systemer eller eksperimentelle møter med teknologiske objekter. Muligheter for praksisbasert eksperimentering kan inkludere arbeid med intelligente systemer og forskningsutstyr som Hypnotic AI, der dette er relevant og gjennomførbart. Tilgang til utstyr, laboratoriefasiliteter og bestemte systemer avhenger av nærmere avtale og tilgjengelighet.

Stipendiaten forventes å presentere forskningen sin på faglige arrangementer, delta aktivt i senterets forskningsaktiviteter og publisere eller på andre måter formidle forskningsresultater gjennom relevante vitenskapelige publiserings- og formidlingskanaler, inkludert åpen publisering der det er mulig.

• Masteroppgave med et omfang tilsvarende 30 studiepoeng eller mer hvis søkeren har en mastergrad på 120 studiepoeng.
• Masteroppgave med et omfang tilsvarende 20 studiepoeng eller mer hvis søkeren har en integrert mastergrad på 300 studiepoeng.
 
 
For å bli tatt opp er det krav om et karaktersnitt tilsvarende B eller bedre på mastergraden. Karaktersnittet gjelder også for integrerte 5-årige mastergradsprogram der alle emnene inngår i beregningen. Nærmere beskrivelse av opptakskrav finner du her.

Hvis du oppfyller opptakskravene og blir ansatt i stillingen, vil du samtidig få midlertidig opptak til ph.d.-programmet. Søknad om endelig opptak må leveres senest to måneder etter tiltredelse i stillingen.

For søkere med utenlandsk utdanningsbakgrunn vil det vurderes om utdanningen likestilles med norsk høyere utdanning på mastergradsnivå. Vurderingen følger nasjonal godkjenningspraksis, se Direktoratet for høyere utdanning og kompetanse. Søkere med utdanning fra enkelte land må ha mer høyere utdanning for å fylle opptakskravene, for eksempel 4-årig bachelor og 2-årig master. UiT godkjenner normalt utenlandsk høyere utdanning fra land som har ratifisert Lisboakonvensjonen.
Inkluderende arbeidsliv og mangfold  
UiT Norges arktiske universitet har et personalpolitisk mål om å være en arbeidsgiver som gjenspeiler mangfoldet i samfunnet og som tar i bruk potensialet i befolkningens samlede kompetanse. Vi mener at inkludering og mangfold er en styrke og ønsker oss medarbeidere med ulik kompetanse, fagkombinasjoner, livserfaring og perspektiver.   

Har du funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn, oppfordrer vi deg som søker til å krysse av for dette i jobbsøkerportalen. Er det kvalifiserte søkere, kaller vi inn minst én i hver gruppe til intervju, og får du jobben, legger vi til rette for deg om du trenger det. Utenom å velge ut riktige kandidater bruker vi ikke avkrysningene til noe annet enn anonymisert statistikk. Les mer i Arbeidsgiverportalen: arbeidsgiver.difi.no/positivsaerbehandling  
Vi tilbyr
• Du blir en del av et spennende forskningsmiljø
• Gode karrieremuligheter 
• Et godt arbeidsmiljø med dedikerte kolleger  
• Gode velferdsordninger  
• Gode pensjons-, forsikrings-, og låneordninger i Statens pensjonskasse
• Stipendiater får normalt 580 000,- i årslønn med 3% økning pr. år
• Mulighet for å søke om stipend for et lengre forskningsopphold i utlandet
• Mulighet til å bli en del av et aktivt og tverrfaglig forskningsmiljø ved Senter for kvinne- og kjønnsforskning (SKK)
• Gode muligheter for faglig samarbeid og kunnskapsutveksling på tvers av kjønnsforskning, kritiske teknologistudier og KI-forskning.
• Mulighet til å søke om finansiering av forskningsopphold i utlandet og bygge internasjonale forskningsnettverk. 
• Tett faglig oppfølging og veiledning gjennom doktorgradsløpet
• Et inkluderende og støttende arbeidsmiljø med engasjerte kolleger
• Mulighet for fysisk aktivitet i arbeidstidenSøknaden
Vær oppmerksom på at søknaden kun vurderes basert på vedleggene som er sendt inn innen søknadsfristen via Jobbnorge. Det er derfor viktig at du legger ved alle nødvendige dokumenter som viser dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen.

Søknaden din må inneholde:  

• Søknadsbrev med beskrivelse av dine forskningsinteresser og motivasjon for stillingen 
• CV 
• Offisielle vitnemål for bachelor- og mastergrad på originalspråk
• Offisielle karakterutskrifter for bachelor- og mastergrad på originalspråk
• Offisiell oversettelse av vitnemål og karakterutskrifter til engelsk eller et skandinavisk språk, hvis aktuelt
• Forklaring på karaktersystemet for utenlandsk utdanning (Diploma Supplement om tilgjengelig) 
• Dokumentasjon av engelskkunnskaper 
• 2-3 referanser med kontaktinformasjon 
• Masteroppgaven, og eventuelle andre vitenskapelige arbeider 
• Prosjektbeskrivelse (8-10 sider, inkludert referanse) 
Søkere skal ha dokumentert gode kunnskaper i engelsk, og kunne jobbe i et internasjonalt miljø. Nordiske søkere kan dokumentere dette med vitnemål fra videregående skole. 

Søkere må ha mastergrad før tiltredelse i stillingen. Kandidater som er i sluttfasen av mastergraden, oppfordres også til å søke. I slike tilfeller må søkerne legge ved et utkast til masteroppgaven, en oppdatert karakterutskrift og en bekreftelse fra veileder eller institusjon som angir forventet tidspunkt for fullføring av graden. Mastergraden må være fullført før den som får tilbud om stillingen, tiltrer.

All dokumentasjon som skal vurderes må være på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. Hvis dokumentasjon på engelskkunnskaper mangler på søknadstidspunktet, må det dokumenteres før tiltredelse. 
Bedømmelse
Søkerne vil bli vurdert av en sakkyndig komité. Komiteens mandat er å foreta en vurdering av søkernes kvalifikasjoner på grunnlag av søknadsdokumentene og kunngjøringsteksten. Alle søkere vil motta en kopi av vurderingen til den sakkyndige komitéen. 

Søkere som vurderes å være best kvalifisert vil bli innkalt til intervju. Intervjuet skal blant annet avklare personlig egnethet og motivasjon for stillingen. 
Generell informasjon 
Ansettelsen skjer i henhold til regler og vilkår som til enhver tid gjelder for statsansatte, og retningslinjer ved UiT. På våre nettsider finner du mer informasjon til søkere på stillinger ved UiT. 

Stilling som stipendiat lønnes etter statens regulativ kode 1017. Fra lønnen blir det trukket 2% innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse.Du vil bli medlem i Statens pensjonskasse, som gir deg mange goder i tillegg til livsvarig alderspensjon og AFP: Du kan ha rett til økonomisk støtte hvis du blir syk eller ufør, familien din kan ha rett til økonomisk støtte når du dør, du blir forsikret mot yrkesskade eller yrkessykdom, og du får gode betingelser på boliglån. Les mer om ansattgodene dine på: spk.no.
 
Kortere ansettelsesperiode kan gis dersom stipendiaten alt har gjennomført deler av sitt forskerutdanningsprogram, eller når ansettelsen bygger på tidligere ansettelse i utdanningsstilling, slik at total tid til forskerutdanning blir tre år. 

Personopplysninger som oppgis behandles i henhold til lov om behandling av personopplysninger. Søkere kan be om ikke å bli oppført på den offentlige søkerlista, men universitetet kan likevel beslutte at navnet på søkeren skal offentliggjøres. Søkeren vil da bli varslet i forkant av offentliggjøring.  

Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT Norges arktiske universitet er et internasjonalt ledende breddeuniversitet. Vår visjon er å være en drivkraft i nord. Det nordsamiske begrepet eallju, som betyr arbeidsiver, setter tonen for drivkraften i UiT. Sammen med studenter, ansatte og samfunnet for øvrig skal vi utnytte vår beliggenhet i Nord-Norge og Sápmi, vår faglige bredde og tverrfaglige fortrinn til å forme framtiden. 

UiT har om lag 18 000 studenter, mer enn 4000 ansatte, og er etablert på fire hovedcampuser og sju øvrige studiesteder i Nord-Norge og på Svalbard. Våre største campuser er Tromsø, Alta, Narvik og Harstad. UiT har sju fakulteter, 40 institutter og sentre, og ledende forskningsmiljøer innenfor ulike fag. Universitetet har 269 studieprogrammer og har fokus på utdanningskvalitet. 

Akademisk frihet, vitenskapelige og forskningsetiske prinsipper ligger til grunn for hele UiT sin virksomhet. Medvirkning, medbestemmelse, åpenhet og gode prosesser skal gi det beslutningsgrunnlaget vi trenger for å gjøre kloke og framsynte prioriteringer.  Våre studenter og ansatte skal ha mulighet til å utvikle sine evner og potensial. Tuftet på vitenskapelig integritet skal vi være modige, engasjerte og rause - tett på fag, folk og samtidsutviklingen.

jobs.description:
About the position
A fixed-term 100 % position as a PhD Research Fellow in Civil and Structural Engineering, is available at the University of Agder, Faculty of Engineering and Science. The position is affiliated with the Department of Engineering Sciences and is offered for a period of three years. The position is located at Campus Grimstad. The starting date is agreed with the Faculty.

The Department of Engineering Sciences has more than 120 employees in scientific positions and more than 1500 students at all levels. A wide range of research activities is conducted across the department’s research groups: Mechatronics, Renewable Energy, Civil Engineering, and Industrial Economy. Interdisciplinary projects within the department or with other research groups are also welcome.

This position will be affiliated with the Civil Engineering section. The department has extensive international collaboration and works closely with industrial partners and public-sector organisations in the region. These collaborations provide valuable opportunities for both teaching and research. Our partners contribute assignments, expertise and resources.

Project background

The position is associated with a recently awarded EU project, HelioSea. The project aims to develop innovative interconnected floating solar arrays for offshore sites. The project will assess innovative concepts under various environmental conditions, investigate systems integration and the co-location of different marine renewable energy devices, and conduct techno-economic analyses.
Responsibilities
The PhD research fellow will conduct research on the design and analysis of multibody floating solar systems under offshore environmental conditions. Such systems are typically characterised by lightweight floats with mechanical connectors and mooring systems.

The work will involve analytical modelling and numerical analysis of multibody hydrodynamics. Structural analysis may also be included, depending on the research focus. The candidate is expected to work collaboratively in an international research environment.

The research will include preparing and submitting research reports, publishing high-quality scientific articles, and participating in dissemination activities at the European level.
Required qualifications
Applicants must hold a master’s degree in Marine Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field. Applicants must have their master’s thesis approved by the application deadline.

Applicants are expected to have in-depth knowledge of several of the following subjects:

• Marine hydrodynamics
• Structural Dynamics
• Physics-based simulations of marine structures
• Stochastic analysis methods
• Design optimization
As a general rule, the following should normally apply:

• The average grade for courses included in the bachelor's degree (or equivalent) should be C (or equivalent) or higher. 
• The average grade for all courses (including the dissertation) in the master’s degree should be B (or equivalent) or higher. The master's dissertation (or equivalent) should have the grade B (or equivalent) or higher. 
• Competence in English is a requirement for all applicants to the PhD programme. International candidates that are not exempt from the English language requirements pursuant to the guidelines of the Norwegian Agency for Quality Assurance in Education (NOKUT), must document this through one of the following tests with the stated results or better: 
• TOEFL - Test of English as a Foreign Language with a minimum score of 600 for the Paperbased Test (PBT), or 92 for the Internetbased Test (iBT)
• IELTS - International English Language Testing System, with the result of 6.5
Criteria for positions as PhD Research Fellow (in Norwegian).
Desired qualifications
• Research experience and a record of scientific publications
• Strong analytical and programming skills
• Research or work experience related to offshore structuresPersonal qualities
The assessment will place emphasis on personal suitability, teamwork skills and relevant practical experience. Research fellows are expected to contribute to the active research community at the University. The position requires the ability to work independently towards defined goals, maintain focus and pay attention to detail.
We offer
• Professional development in a large, exciting and socially important organisation
• A positive, inclusive and diverse working environment
• Modern facilities and comprehensive welfare schemes
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund 
More about working at UiA.

The position is remunerated according to the State Salary Scale, salary plan 17.515, code 1017 PhD Research Fellow, NOK 550 800 gross salary per year. A compulsory pension contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted from the salary according to current statutory provisions.
General information
UiA is an open and inclusive university. We believe that diversity enriches the workplace and makes us better. We, therefore, encourage qualified candidates to apply for the position independent of gender, age, cultural background, disability or an incomplete CV.

Women are strongly encouraged to apply for the position. 

The successful applicant will have rights and obligations in accordance with the current regulations for the position, and organisational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities of the position must be expected. The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning the acts relating to Control of Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology.

Appointment is made by the University of Agder’s Appointments Committee for Teaching and Research Positions. A background check may be conducted to verify information that appears in available documents. Background checks are always done with the applicant's consent, and employment in the position requires an approved background check. Relevant applicants will receive further information.

Short-listed applicants will be invited for interview. With the applicant’s permission, UiA will also conduct a reference check before appointment. Read more about the employment process.

In accordance with the Freedom of Information Act § 25 (2), applicants may request that they are not identified in the open list of applicants. The University, however, reserves the right to publish the names of applicants. Applicants will be advised of the University’s intention to exercise this right.
Application
Applications, including documentation of education and experience (such as diplomas and certificates), must be submitted electronically via the link “Apply for this job”.

The following documentation must be uploaded electronically:

• Academic transcripts showing grades from bachelor’s and master’s degree programmes
• A CV detailing education and work experience
• Up to 10 academic articles or R&D projects that the candidate wishes to emphasise in the assessment process
• A brief project description related to the research topic described above.  (maximum two pages) The project description should outline proposed research questions, methods and relevance to floating solar arrays.
The applicant is fully responsible for submitting complete digital documentation by the application deadline. All documentation must be available in a Scandinavian language or English.

Application deadline: 01.12.26.
